key_insight: A conditional diffusion model can generate realistic spatiotemporal turbulent flame evolution from experimental OH-PLIF and PIV data, including unseen transition events.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven surrogate for studying flame dynamics and regime transitions when experiments are sparse or expensive, complementing CFD and laboratory measurements.
method: x-prediction flow matching for conditional diffusion
Pixel-based spatiotemporal transformer to generate entire flame slabs
Transition synthesis via time-varying mixing of attached and detached denoising velocities
evidence_signal: The generated flames preserved key features and statistical consistency across space and time, especially at large scales, and were evaluated on attached/detached states plus liftoff/reattachment transitions.
watch_item: High temporal frequencies and small spatial scales showed deviations that depend on the generated slab length, so short-horizon fidelity may be limited.
paper_title: Generating synthetic evolution of turbulent flames with an experimental data-based spatiotemporal diffusion model
